name: Demo: Appèl, Aula student use
problemOwnerDescription: Owns all FoodCity community activity: events, the FoodCity app and Instagram. She pushed for the Aula seating-area renovation herself, and her goal is community, not sales. A colleague takes over after December and implements the ideas. TU Delft's space manager (who runs the seating area) attends the whole morning and sometimes has budget left.
problemAsGiven: How can we better align the Aula with students' needs and make them more aware of the different possibilities the space offers, so that students use the Aula more frequently throughout the day?
introduction: The Aula is full at lunch and nearly empty before and after. Before COVID it was where students met; each new cohort since never learned that habit. The new seating area (couches, game corner, small tables) opens 4 January 2027. Furniture, layout and power sockets are fixed. In scope: low-cost things to add, making students aware they're welcome (own food is allowed, no need to buy anything), and daily reasons to come, by time window (morning, afternoon, evening: the Aula is the only FoodCity dinner spot). Session runs in the Aula itself, Mon 12 Oct, 09:00-11:30. Output for the colleague who takes over in January: ideas with an owner, a cost level and a first step for January.
description: A real IDEM104 client session (TU Delft, 12 Oct 2026): how might Appèl get students to use the Aula outside lunch? 135 minutes for an RG of 6, from the welcome to the concept posters. Open it to see a finished plan, or run it live to try the timer.
